avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Magnesium potentiates neuromuscular blockade by inhibiting acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplemental magnesium during rocuronium therapy; monitor serum magnesium levels

avoid_supplements.name: Aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Synergistic potentiation of neuromuscular blockade; reduces acetylcholine release
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; ensure no concomitant aminoglycoside use during rocuronium administration

avoid_supplements.name: Fluoroquinolone supplements
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use with close neuromuscular monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Calcium may antagonize neuromuscular blockade; separate administration timing
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blockade duration; administer calcium away from rocuronium dosing

caution_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Hyperkalemia risk post-rocuronium administration; rocuronium may increase serum potassium
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum potassium; avoid supplementation unless clinically indicated

avoid_foods.name: High-potassium foods (bananas, spinach, avocado)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Rocuronium can cause hyperkalemia, particularly in trauma/burn patients; excessive dietary potassium increases risk
avoid_foods.action: Limit high-potassium foods during perioperative period; monitor serum potassium

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may theoretically alter rocuronium metabolism minimally; rocuronium undergoes primarily renal elimination
caution_foods.action: No strict restriction needed; general caution advised in hepatically impaired patients

monitoring_notes: Rocuronium is primarily renounced via renal elimination (Hofmann elimination) with minimal hepatic metabolism, reducing traditional drug-supplement interactions. Close neuromuscular monitoring is essential, particularly in patients with renal impairment, magnesium abnormalities, or concurrent neuromuscular-potentiating agents.
